blocks.text:
After breakfast at 10:00, visit the train cemetery, where old steam locomotives once used to carry minerals stand.

Continue to Colchani to see how salt is dried, ground and packaged and to buy salt handicrafts if you wish. On the salt flat, see the salt mounds, natural springs and the Salt Museum, which is built entirely of salt blocks.

Lunch is served in the centre of the salt flat. The route continues to Incahuasi Island, where giant cacti grow, some more than 100 years old. The summit has sweeping views over the salt flat. On the way to the island, you’ll see the salt mounds, places where groundwater comes to the surface and the Salt Museum. In Colchani you can follow the entire salt processing cycle, from drying to grinding and packaging.

After crossing the salt flat from north to south, follow a chain of volcanoes to Lípez, with a view of Ollagüe Volcano. Within a single day the white expanse of Uyuni gives way to dry desert, volcanoes and high-altitude lakes. Continue to Eduardo Avaroa National Reserve and the Cañapa, Hedionda and Honda lagoons, where three Andean flamingo species occur. Overnight at Hotel Los Flamencos, with dinner at the hotel.
